statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-114148 is a .NET elevation of privilege issue: Linux .NET tarballs, including every tarball produced by source-build, carried incorrect file ownership, so an extraction that preserves numeric ownership can leave runtime files that a local account controls. Microsoft lists source-built .NET 9 Linux distributions from 9.0.100 up to but not including 9.0.123 as affected and 9.0.123 (.NET 9.0.22) as fixed; the fix makes source-build create its tarballs with normalized numeric ownership (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/495, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/70040, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.22/9.0.22.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 is a source build of .NET 9 for Linux, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 9.0.22-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v9.0.123 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v9.0.123), and its assemblies record that tag's commit, 9f04b57. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0 through 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every file and directory in every package is owned by root (0:0), none is group- or world-writable, and none of the packages contains a .tar.gz or .tar.xz archive. The decision follows Microsoft's source-build boundary: builds before 9.0.22-r0 come from source releases without the fix, and the range ends at 9.0.22-r0, the first published build made from the fixed release.
